title: Social Safety Net for Disabled who Need Institutional Long-term Care Beyond ElderShield
what_it_is: Social Safety Net for Disabled who Need Institutional Long-term Care Beyond ElderShield

sections.label: Long-term care social safety net
sections.summary: Singapore provides insurance schemes, subsidies, MediFund, MediSave withdrawals, ElderFund and other assistance for severely disabled persons needing long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health what social safety net is there for a person who remains severely disabled and requires institutional long-term care even after the six years under ElderShield.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These include insurance schemes, such as ElderShield, Government subsidies and assistance schemes, especially for those with less means, personal and family savings, for instance, and also Central Provident Fund retirement payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Singaporeans can tap on Government subsidies of up to 75% of nursing home costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Singaporeans who require additional financial assistance for institutional care in nursing homes can tap on Government-funded safety nets, such as MediFund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: From 2020, Singaporeans can benefit from new initiatives to defray the cost of long-term care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These are (a) CareShield Life, a new long-term care insurance scheme which provides monthly cash benefits for the severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The scheme will cover all Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, regardless of whether they have pre-existing disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Those born in 1979 or earlier and not severely disabled can join CareShield Life in 2021; (b) next, all severely disabled Singaporeans above the age of 30, including those who have finished their ElderShield payouts, will be able to withdraw up to $200 per month in cash from their or their spouse's MediSave; and finally, we will introduce ElderFund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: This will be a new discretionary assistance scheme which provides up to $250 per month for low-income severely disabled citizens who are unable to join CareShield Life, have low MediSave balances and face financial difficulties in meeting their long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And if special consideration, in the discretion of the Ministry, could be applied to those who are actually suffering from severe disabilities now, and have used up the six years of ElderShield and, therefore, need a leg up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I will add that apart from what I mentioned, there are also other assistance schemes, such as the Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly, which provides means-tested payouts of up to $200 per month for six years.
